column1: #build label(roller_line) start(1; 1) message(A powered roller conveyor. A water wheel drives a horizontal axle into a gear assembly
column2: and the gear powers a line of east-facing rollers that push items placed on them to the east. Link a lever to the gear to run the belt on and off. The rollers only move items while powered
column3: so the whole train must form a connected power path back to the wheel.)

column1: title: Powered roller conveyor (rollers and axles)
tags: build, machine, roller, axle, power, hauling
description: A minimal powered conveyor that shows the roller and axle tokens the screw-pump example did not cover. Mw is a water wheel built over moving water; it feeds Mh
column4: a gear assembly. From the gear
column5: a line of rollerEW rollers carries power east and pushes any item set on them one tile east per cycle. Rollers are directional: rollerEW moves items east
column8: rollerSN north. Each roller takes a speed property from 50000 (fastest) down to 10000 (slowest); 50000 is used here. The gear assembly Mg is the junction you link a lever (Tl) to
column9: so you can start and stop the belt without deconstructing it. To carry power across a Z-level use Mv
column11: and to run an axle north-south use Mhs instead of Mh. Placement rules the blueprint cannot enforce: the water wheel must sit over flowing water
column12: every machine must form a connected power path back to a power source
column13: and the wheel plus rollers draw power that the source has to supply. Lengthen the belt by painting more rollerEW tiles
column14: or branch power off the gear with another axle run.
